subject: Edge data-plane control — SLA exception request for customer-managed gateways
messages:
From: Emily Song <emily.song@quantaforge.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@quantaforge.com
Date: 2028-09-18T09:12:00Z
Subject: Request: SLA exception for customer-managed edge gateways

Hi Ben,

Thanks for taking this. As discussed in yesterday's call, QuantaForge will continue to operate a set of customer-managed edge gateways that handle customer traffic termination before it reaches Redwood Private connectors. Because these gateways are under our ops control (on-prem in several customer sites), we need a formal exception to the standard latency and uptime SLA that assumes end-to-end control by Redwood.

Key asks:
- An explicit clause acknowledging that latency and packet loss attributable to customer-controlled edge gateways are excluded from Redwood's availability/latency SLOs.
- A defined process for evidence submission (syslogs/pcaps/monitoring snapshots) and a 10-business-day validation window for attributions.
- Guidance on minimum observability we should enable so Redwood can reliably attribute faults (preferred metrics and log formats).

I've attached our maintenance calendar and an architecture diagram to help with scope. Happy to walk through these with engineering.

Attachments: quantaforge-maintenance-calendar.csv (CSV), edge-architecture-diagram.pdf (diagram)

Best,
Emily Song
Head of Infrastructure
QuantaForge

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Emily Song <emily.song@quantaforge.com>
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: 2028-09-18T13:42:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: SLA exception for customer-managed edge gateways

Thanks Emily — appreciate the context and the artifacts, they help a lot. Looping in Soojin (security/compliance), Kimberly (account lead), and Aditya (support/ops) to scope the exception and the operational playbook.

High-level I think we can accommodate an exclusion for customer-controlled termination points, but we need to capture three operational controls before legal will sign off:
1) Evidence protocol: a minimal list of items you will provide for attribution requests (timestamped syslog slices, sampled pcap, APM/agent traces) and a canonical format (CSV/JSON + PCAP).
2) Observability contract: which metrics and export cadence you can reasonably promise (e.g., interface drop counters per 10s, latency histograms per 1 minute, and a heartbeat every 30s).
3) Dispute timeline and rollback: we propose a 10-business-day investigation window and an automated temporary fallback to Redwood-managed connectors if there is a sustained impact for >3 hours during business hours.

Can you confirm whether Quantaforge can supply the metrics above and whether the maintenance calendar represents any recurring windows we should encode into the exception? If yes, we will draft proposed wording for inclusion in the Private deployment SOW and an operational playbook appendix.

Also note: if you need a permanent SLA carveout (rather than per-incident attribution), Legal will require a short appendix listing exact IP ranges/hostnames under your control and an executed attestation of the maintenance process.

Next steps: Emily, can you confirm capabilities and any constraints by EOD Thursday (2028-09-21)? We'll aim to circulate draft clause the following week.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Account Exec, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

From: Emily Song <emily.song@quantaforge.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@quantaforge.com, contracts@quantaforge.com
Date: 2028-09-19T11:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: SLA exception for customer-managed edge gateways

Ben — thanks. Quick responses inline below.

Evidence protocol: yes, we can supply timestamped syslog slices (RFC5424) and PCAPs for sampled windows. We can produce a zipped bundle with a small manifest JSON that includes UTC timestamps and the collector hostname.

Observability contract: we can export:
- interface.drop.count (1s counters, we can aggregate to 10s/1m)
- tcp.connect.latency (p99/median histograms per 1m)
- dataplane.heartbeat (30s heartbeat ping)
We currently run these collectors in our customers' edge gateways (agent v3.2). We'll add the manifest header and canonical CSV export if Redwood confirms schema.

Maintenance windows: the attached calendar is both recurring and ad-hoc windows; standard weekly maintenance is Tue 02:00–04:00 UTC for 30% of sites, and monthly patching windows on the first Sat of the month. We can mark exceptions for critical sites.

Regarding fallback: we are amenable to the 3-hour sustained-impact trigger for automatic Redwood fallback, but we need an explicit rollback playbook so that our customers aren't surprised by traffic re-routing.

I've attached a sample evidence bundle (link in Drive) and can share a Redacted PCAP on request.

Attachments: quantaforge-maintenance-calendar.csv, edge-architecture-diagram.pdf

Let us know the schema you want for the CSV manifest and we'll produce a sample by EOD.

—Emily

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Emily Song <emily.song@quantaforge.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: 2028-09-20T16:47:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: SLA exception for customer-managed edge gateways

Hi Emily / Ben — thanks for the quick back-and-forth. From a security/compliance and contract perspective we can accept an operational exclusion for customer-controlled edge gateways under the following conditions (these are prerequisites for Legal to sign the appendix):

1) Enumerated scope: a definitive list of IP ranges/hostnames and a site roster for any customer-managed gateways that will be excluded (CSV).
2) Evidence manifest: the bundle must include UTC timestamps, hostname, collector version, and MD5 hashes for attached PCAPs; accepted formats: RFC5424 syslog, PCAP v2, and a manifest.json (we'll accept a JSON or CSV manifest).
3) Observability minimums: interface drop counters (1s granularity), latency histograms (1m), and dataplane heartbeats (30s). Export frequency must be documented in the appendix.
4) Incident timeline: Redwood and QuantaForge will follow a 10-business-day attribution window. If attribution cannot be determined within that window, incidents default to a mitigated shared-status while we continue joint investigation.
4) Fallback and customer notice: any automatic switchover to Redwood-managed connectors requires a 30-minute pre-switch notification to the QuantaForge on-call and an immediate post-switch incident summary.
5) Data retention: evidence for attribution requests must be retained for 90 days.

If you can provide the scope CSV plus a sample manifest by 2028-09-25, Legal will draft the appendix language and a DocuSign packet for execution. We'll also include an operational playbook template for the rollback/notification flow.

If convenient, Aditya can set up a short triage call to run through the export schema next week.

Sooj
Soojin Lee
Head of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
